findings.title: Lack of Memory Limits on Decompression
findings.description: When decompressing, the library allocates a buffer based on the `size` field in the central header without verifying if the available system memory is sufficient, leading to potential out-of-memory errors.
steps_to_exploit: Create a zip archive with an entry reporting an extremely large `size` (e.g., several GBs).
Call the decompression method on that entry.
The library attempts to allocate the requested size in RAM, crashing the process.
findings.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) via memory exhaustion.

findings.title: Implicit Trust in Zip Header Metadata
findings.description: The library relies heavily on metadata provided within the zip file (like `size` and `compressedSize`) to perform memory allocations and file operations without secondary verification.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a zip file with conflicting header information (e.g., local header size vs central directory size).
The library may attempt to read past buffer bounds or allocate incorrect memory blocks during extraction.
Potential for buffer overflow or out-of-bounds read vulnerabilities in underlying Node.js calls.
findings.impact: Potential memory corruption or process crash.
